payload.use_cases:
FOUR USE CASES, every story covered.

UC-A CONSULT A SOURCE THE PROCESS REQUIRES (covers S1, S3). Scope: the read and search lane plus the packet. Level: user-goal. Primary actor: the walking agent. Trigger: a step whose guidance names a source.
MAIN SCENARIO: 1. the agent receives its packet, which carries the step's instruction AND every rule that applies to it, resolved. 2. the agent identifies the source it must consult - a document, a v1 file, a closed iteration's evidence. 3. it asks for the part it needs rather than the whole. 4. the lane returns that part, with enough surrounding context to read the ruling around a hit. 5. the agent works from what the source says. 6. the log records what was consulted, by name.
EXTENSIONS: 3a. the source is larger than one response - the lane returns the requested range and says how much remains, never silently truncating. 3b. the source is outside the repository - it is addressed by a declared name, or the lane refuses with a remedy that declares it. 3c. the source exists only in history - the lane searches refs, not the working tree. 4a. no match - the lane says so; it never answers a different question. 4b. the request is malformed (a wrong argument name) - the lane REFUSES; it never coerces a missing value into a plausible search. 6a. the source is outside the product - the read is still logged, though it is not a product mutation.

UC-B CHANGE MANY PLACES AT ONCE (covers S4). Scope: the write lane. Level: user-goal. Primary actor: the walking agent. Trigger: one mechanical change with several sites.
MAIN SCENARIO: 1. the agent locates every site. 2. it sends one call carrying all edits, each with its own guard. 3. the lane applies them atomically. 4. the record shows one provenanced change.
EXTENSIONS: 2a. one edit's guard fails - NOTHING applies, and the response names which one and why. 2b. an edit matches more than once - refused, as today, rather than guessing. 3a. the agent is tempted to script the change instead - it is faster through the lane, which is the whole design; if it is not, the tool has failed and that is reportable under the workaround law.

UC-C ADJUDICATE A GATE WHOSE MECHANICAL HALF IS COMPUTED (covers S2, S6). Scope: the machine, the evidence forms, the lint layer. Level: user-goal. Primary actor: the walking agent; secondary: the owner-as-auditor, later.
MAIN SCENARIO: 1. the agent reaches a gate. 2. the machine runs every lint the gate declares. 3. each lint DECIDES - pass or fail - and its verdict is recorded as the field's evidence. 4. the agent fills only the fields requiring judgement. 5. it blesses under the standing grant, or the owner blesses. 6. the grant records which checks were computed and which asserted, distinguishably.
EXTENSIONS: 2a. a lint cannot decide - it DEFERS, and the check appears as prose exactly as today; the run never waits. 3a. a lint fails - the gate does not open, and the failure names the fact that did not hold, not an opinion. 3b. a lint fails WRONGLY - the agent reports it under the workaround law; a wrong lint is a defect to remove, never a cost to absorb. 5a. the run is unattended - it proceeds; the slider reaching zero is the design, not a degraded mode.

UC-D KEEP THE RECORD FINDABLE (covers S5). Scope: the close, the git lane. Level: subfunction. Primary actor: the engine at close; secondary: the owner, pushing.
MAIN SCENARIO: 1. an iteration closes. 2. the close names the evidence commit by HASH in the grant, not only by a tag name. 3. it creates an annotated tag, so a flag-carrying push takes it. 4. it deletes the iteration branch, which also removes the branch-and-tag name ambiguity git already warns about. 5. later, a search over the record finds evidence in a ref that no working tree contains.
EXTENSIONS: 2a. the tag is deleted by anyone - the evidence is still reachable by hash from trunk, because the merge's second parent holds it. 3a. the remote already carries a lightweight tag of that name - completing the migration needs a force-push, which is an owner act and ships as a handover step, never a quiet rewrite. 5a. the ref name is ambiguous - it is not, once step 4 has run; this is why step 4 is load-bearing rather than housekeeping.
